item.title: Lutein & Zeaxanthin
item.description:
What it is: Lutein and zeaxanthin are carotenoid antioxidants concentrated in the macula (central retina) that protect against light-induced damage and oxidative stress. Research shows supplementation reduces age-related macular degeneration (AMD) risk—the leading cause of vision loss in aging.

Benefits

Eye Health & Vision

  • Accumulates in macula (protective pigment)
  • Reduces glare sensitivity
  • Improves visual comfort and clarity
  • Supports contrast sensitivity
  • Enhances color vision

Macular Degeneration Prevention

  • Reduces AMD (age-related macular degeneration) risk
  • Protects against vision loss with aging
  • Slows AMD progression if present
  • Best evidence for age-related vision protection
  • Particularly valuable for those 50+

Antioxidant Protection

  • Protects retina from oxidative damage
  • Filters harmful blue light
  • Reduces photooxidative stress
  • Supports overall eye health

Cognitive Benefits (Emerging)

  • Lutein crosses blood-brain barrier
  • May support cognitive function
  • Brain antioxidant protection
  • Emerging brain health benefits

Dosage

Vision support: 10-15 mg daily Enhanced AMD prevention: 15-20 mg daily Timing: With meals containing fat (enhances absorption) Duration: 8-12 weeks for initial effects; 12+ weeks for full benefits

item.title: Vitamin B3 (Niacin)
item.description:
What Is Vitamin B3 (Niacin)?

Vitamin B3, also known as niacin, nicotinic acid, or vitamin PP (pellagra-preventing), exists as multiple chemical entities with different biochemical functions and biohacking implications. Understanding these distinctions is critical for optimizing outcomes:

Nicotinic Acid (Niacin): The original form recognized to prevent pellagra (severe deficiency disease); provides the flush response and most potent therapeutic effects on lipid profiles and NAD+ elevation.

Nicotinamide (Niacinamide): The non-flushing form; functions as a direct NAD+ precursor but lacks the lipid-modifying and flushing effects of nicotinic acid—important distinction for protocol selection.

item.title: CoQ10
item.description:
What Is CoQ10?

Coenzyme Q10 (CoQ10), also called ubiquinone, is a naturally occurring coenzyme found in every cell in your body. It’s essential for:

  1. ATP Production — the energy currency of cells
  2. Antioxidant Defense — protecting cells from oxidative damage
  3. Cellular Signaling — regulating important biological processes

While your body produces CoQ10, production declines with age (dropping 50% by age 60) and is depleted by certain medications, particularly statins.

CoQ10 is especially critical for high-energy organs: the heart, brain, liver, and kidneys.

item.title: HMB (Beta-Hydroxy Beta-Methylbutyrate)
item.description:
What Is HMB?

HMB (Beta-Hydroxy Beta-Methylbutyrate) is a metabolite of the essential branched-chain amino acid leucine. Your body naturally produces about 0.2-0.4 grams of HMB daily from dietary leucine, but supplemental doses provide significantly greater anti-catabolic effects.

HMB is one of the most researched supplements for preventing muscle breakdown with over 50 peer-reviewed studies demonstrating its effectiveness, particularly during caloric restriction, intense training, or periods of physical stress.

Benefits

Primary Benefits

  • Muscle Preservation: Prevents muscle breakdown during caloric deficit
  • Anti-Catabolic Effects: Reduces protein degradation via ubiquitin-proteasome pathway
  • Faster Recovery: Reduces exercise-induced muscle damage
  • Strength Maintenance: Preserves strength during cutting phases

Secondary Benefits

  • Reduced Muscle Soreness: Less DOMS (delayed onset muscle soreness)
  • Improved Endurance: May enhance aerobic capacity
  • Fat Loss Support: Helps preserve metabolic rate during dieting
  • Aging Support: Combats sarcopenia in older adults
  • Immune Function: May support immune health during intense training
